text:
Marta L: FYI we just received a chargeback from Acme Corp for invoice INV-2026-045 — $14,200. They claim "unauthorized usage" and want evidence. Stripe dispute ID dp_1Jk9Xx. We have 7 days to respond. cc @Alex H @Raj P
Alex H: Thanks. Do we have the customer's email on file and the card last4? Also which project and timeframe?
Marta L: Customer email is finance@acme.example, card last4 4242, timeframe billed 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-14. Charge described as "API usage" on invoice.
Raj P: Can someone attach the usage breakdown? Need per-day token counts, model name, and request IPs for that window.
Olivia (CS): I pinged the CS rep on the account — they'll pull any contract emails.
Stripe-Bot: dispute.created id=dp_1Jk9Xx amount=14200 currency=USD reason=fraud created=1714208700
SupportBot: Ticket #FT-3291 created to collect logs. Assigning to @Raj P and @Alex H.
Alex H: Raj, can you pull the following from query logs for 2026-05-01..2026-05-14: request_id, project_id, billing_project, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, ip_address, api_key_id. Prefer CSV. Example SQL below:
```
SELECT request_id, project_id, billing_project, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, ip_address, api_key_id, ts
FROM request_logs
WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-05-01' AND '2026-05-14' AND billing_project = 'acme-prod-01';
```
Raj P: On it. Will also cross-check KV cache hits and any anomalous batching spikes.
Marta L: Also need any onboarding emails or user confirmation that API key creation was authorized by their admin. Olivia, any luck?
Olivia (CS): CS says they have an onboarding thread where they added user "sam.green@acme.example" on 2026-04-28 and created two API keys. Sharing link: https://cs.example/acme/onboarding-thread (internal).
Alex H: If the keys were legitimately created from an IP range not matching the billing address, that's not necessarily fraud, but we should document it. Also check for region mismatch (e.g., sudden calls from SE Asia).
Raj P: Quick summary from logs: 2026-05-03 had a burst of 2.1M tokens over 6 hours from ip 34.82.10.45, model rdx-7b-q, api_key_id key_abc123. Most calls show consistent user-agent "redwood-client/1.2.0". I'll attach CSV in the ticket.
Marta L: Thanks. CS says the admin confirms they didn't authorize volume that high. They asked for a provisional refund and to put the account on hold until resolved. Thoughts?
Alex H: We should flag the account (account_hold=true) and block the active API keys to prevent further spend. Legal probably prefers we gather evidence first before issuing refunds. Also open a fraud case with payments ops.
Olivia (CS): I've already created an internal hold: account placed in 'billing-review' state and we've disabled write keys. Notified the customer.
SupportBot: Actions logged: hold set by Olivia, keys disabled by SupportBot at ts=1714210000.
Marta L: For the dispute response to Stripe, we need: 1) usage CSV 2) key creation logs 3) onboarding confirmation email 4) IP + geo lookup 5) any refund or hold action taken. Can we get all that in 48 hours?
Raj P: I'll drop the CSV and a short analysis (suspicious vs expected) by EOD. IP geo shows 34.82.10.45 -> us-west1. No obvious offshore hop.
Alex H: I'll pull API key creation events and match them to user sessions. If API key was tweeted/leaked etc we need to say so.
Marta L: If we lose the dispute, we'll need to process a chargeback fee and potentially refund. Let's prioritize evidence quality.
Olivia (CS): Customer asked for an interim invoice copy with line items split by model and day — I'm attaching that in the ticket.
Raj P: Uploaded CSV to ticket: https://support.example/tickets/FT-3291/attachment/usage_acme_may.csv (internal). Short finding: volume correlates to a single api_key_id, key created via console by user sam.green on 2026-04-28 14:03 UTC. No password reset or session anomaly recorded.
Alex H: Noted. I'll check session logs for sam.green around key creation time and any IP mismatch.
Marta L: Thank you team. Plan: (a) prepare dispute bundle, (b) keep account on hold, (c) escalate to Legal if CS says customer insists on chargeback. I'll draft the dispute reply for Stripe; Raj and Alex please review.
Stripe-Bot: dispute.updated id=dp_1Jk9Xx status=needs_response by=merchant deadline=1714273200
Raj P: Review done. Minor note: there were 18 requests from 185.62.9.10 in early May — that IP maps to a vpn provider. Marked as suspicious in my notes.
Alex H: If the key was created from corporate IP and later abused from VPN IPs, we can argue key compromise. Provide timeline and we can request chip-and-PIN proof? (jk) Will assemble timeline.
Marta L: Please add short bullet summary for Stripe: who authorized key creation, usage totals, IP timeline, actions taken (hold + keys disabled), attachments list. I'll send reply tomorrow morning.
Olivia (CS): I'll notify the customer contact that we're assembling the response and keep them updated.
Marta L: Closing loop — please add any new artifacts to ticket FT-3291. If we need to issue a provisional goodwill refund, route through me.
Alex H: Added forensic notes to ticket.
Raj P: CSV + timeline uploaded.
Olivia (CS): Customer replied asking for ETA; I said 48 hours.
Marta L: thanks all.
